record.narrative: Initial hypotheses prioritize established dependency logic in lung adenocarcinoma-like cells and binary molecular predictors with adequate cell counts. Negative direction means the exposed group is expected to show stronger dependency (more negative CRISPR score); positive direction means weaker dependency (less negative score). Expected effects include oncogene addiction for KRAS, BRAF V600E, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification; pathway crosstalk effects such as reduced BRAF dependency in KRAS mutants and increased STAT3 dependency with EGFR amplification; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency; TP53-loss/MDM2 synthetic relationship; MSI-high/WRN synthetic lethality; SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 synthetic lethality; and MYC-amplification effects on transcriptional and USP7 dependencies. Analyses are restricted to CRISPR-QC cells and DNA-omics-measured samples to avoid imputed molecular states. All are marked unresolved pending discovery evidence and uncertainty.

Requesting discovery analysis for all 12 registered molecular-marker associations because these are direct, mechanistically motivated tests and all registered comparisons have large enough expected cell sizes within CRISPR-QC DNA-omics-measured samples. These analyses will provide effect sizes, Welch 95% intervals, and cell counts for primary oncogene-addiction and synthetic-lethality hypotheses. Prioritizing these first creates a foundation for later subgroup and refinement analyses.

Discovery evidence strongly supports two mechanistic synthetic-lethal associations: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency and SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. These signed estimates are positive for their negative-direction hypotheses, indicating more negative dependency scores in the exposed groups, and their magnitudes are many multiples of the approximate 10% relative scale based on absolute outcome means. These are accepted as dataset-specific associations; causality and generalizability are not implied. The EGFR amplification-EGFR dependency association is plausible and point size exceeds the 10% threshold, but its lower bound is very close to zero and this was among 12 initial tests, so I keep it unresolved pending independent validation. Most direct oncogene and transcriptional dependencies are small or uncertain. For H2, H3, and H5, the 95% intervals exclude clinically meaningful effects in the registered direction; these are rejected as not supporting the original clinically meaningful associations. H7 is the opposite: KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with a direction opposite to the registered hypothesis, so the original claim is rejected and a reversed claim is proposed for later testing. Several remaining molecular associations remain unresolved because intervals include zero and clinically relevant values.

Independent validation for the EGFR-amplification association with dependency_EGFR (H4) does not support accepting the claim. Discovery R4, signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis, was positive and slightly larger than the approximate 10% relative-difference threshold, but its 95% interval remained very close to zero. Independent validation R13 is signed negative, with a wide interval including zero and both clinically meaningful positive and negative ranges. The two evidence sources are inconsistent, and the validated data do not provide a stable clinically meaningful association; I therefore keep H4 unresolved but close the direct investigation rather than accept it. This does not prove absence; a subgroup effect could remain hidden, so I registered an interaction test between EGFR amplification and KRAS wild-type status.

I also reassessed the reversed KEAP1-loss claim H13. The parent discovery R7 was enormous relative to the NFE2L2 outcome scale: KEAP1-loss cells showed substantially less negative dependency_NFE2L2 than non-loss cells, with the 95% interval entirely on the side of clinically meaningful effect. This strongly supports the reversed dataset-specific association H13, even though the original mechanistic direction H7 was rejected. I accepted H13 and closed its direct investigation.

I reassessed MYC-amplification versus POLR2A dependency H9. Its signed estimate is tiny and the upper confidence limit is below the approximate 10% relative threshold, so I rejected it as not supporting a clinically meaningful difference.

Current supported dataset-specific findings are: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; and KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Current negative findings include rejected KRAS-mutation effects on BRAF dependency, BRAF V600E on BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification on STAT3 dependency, TP53-loss effect on MDM2 dependency in the original direction, and MYC amplification effect on POLR2A dependency. Current unresolved uncertainty includes KRAS mutation on KRAS dependency, ERBB2 amplification on ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency, MYC amplification on USP7 dependency, and EGFR amplification on EGFR dependency. The next analyses focus on heterogeneity of the three strong effects across lineage subtype and constructed research markers, plus one mechanistic EGFR/KRAS subgroup interaction.

Registered new comparisons that refine the three dataset-specific synthetic-lethal/cancer-dependency signals, test their robustness across lineage, library, and culture context, and add mechanistically related broad-exploration tests. For KRAS dependency, the original all-sample association was small and unresolved; a lung adenocarcinoma-only test is a scientifically meaningful refinement. For MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, I registered direct subgroup mean differences within adenocarcinoma to obtain interpretable within-subgroup effect sizes, and interaction tests by lineage subtype, Ky library, and adherent culture to assess whether these large effects are stable or context-specific. The new ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency comparison probes another SWI/SNF complex context, and the KEAP1-loss versus USP7 dependency comparison tests pathway crosstalk around NFE2L2 regulation. All comparisons use CRISPR-QC and DNA-omics-measured cells and are marked unresolved before analysis.

Selecting twelve registered analyses to refine and stress-test the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations while also following up two unresolved mechanistic leads. First, run within-adenocarcinoma mean differences for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss because adenocarcinoma is the dominant lineage and within-subgroup effect estimates are clinically interpretable. Second, run lineage-subtype interaction tests for the same three associations to determine whether these large effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. Third, run CRISPR-library ky interaction tests to assess whether the accepted synthetic-lethal or loss-of-function dependencies remain robust across screen library context. Fourth, run the EGFR-amplification by KRAS-wild-type interaction to investigate whether the inconsistent direct EGFR dependency signal is restricted to a mechanistic subgroup. Finally, run two new mechanistically related comparisons: ARID1A-loss with SMARCA2 dependency, because ARID1A is another SWI/SNF subunit, and KEAP1-loss with USP7 dependency, because it probes pathway crosstalk around the very large KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. These tests maximize information from the newly registered claims without rerunning already estimated primary associations.

The new adenocarcinoma-restricted direct tests strongly confirm the three already accepted dataset-specific dependency associations. For MSI-high versus WRN in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.784 with a narrow 95% interval [0.748, 0.821], far exceeding an approximate 10% threshold based on the WRN score scale; I accept H25 as a dataset-specific subgroup association. For SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.775 [0.752, 0.798], again a very large and precise association; I accept H26. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.795 [0.769, 0.820], accepting H27 as the same reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 relationship seen in the full eligible sample.

The lineage-subtype interaction tests mostly do not show strong evidence that the main effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. H15 rejects an SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 subtype interaction because the signed interval excludes clinically meaningful support in the claimed direction. H14 and H16 have signed point estimates near zero or opposite to the claimed direction, but their intervals include clinically meaningful values in the claimed direction, so I keep them unresolved but deferred rather than claiming precise absence. These are same-dataset subgroup contrasts, not independent validation, and they involve multiplicity and uneven cell sizes.

Library ky context tests are informative. H28 shows no clinically meaningful ky interaction for MSI-high/WRN because the signed interval excludes meaningful support in the claimed direction; reject and close. H30 for KEAP1/NFE2L2 is near zero and opposite to the claimed direction, though imprecise, so I leave it unresolved but deferred. H29 is the one notable borderline finding: the signed SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 ky interaction is +0.044 [ -0.003, 0.091], just around the approximate 10% SMARCA2 scale threshold. The interval crosses zero and includes both negligible and meaningful values, so it cannot support a stable library-context modification; I keep H29 active and propose a direct ky-subgroup SMARCA2 test to clarify it. I also propose direct ky tests for WRN and NFE2L2 to interpret the small imprecise ky interaction estimates.

The EGFR-amplification interaction within KRAS wild-type cells, H20, does not support the failed direct EGFR dependency signal: the signed estimate is small and opposite, though the interval is wide enough to include a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. Given the earlier inconsistent validation for H4, I defer further EGFR subgroup work. ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency is negligible, H34, and KEAP1-loss versus USP7 dependency, H35, is small and imprecise; both remain unresolved only because intervals include some clinically meaningful values, but they are low priority. I request independent validation for H11 because MSI-high/WRN is a large, mechanistically meaningful synthetic-lethal signal with relatively small MSI-high exposure count in discovery, and external validation would strengthen the accepted association. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or guaranteed generalizable findings.

The newly delivered independent validation for H11 strongly supports the MSI-high association with stronger WRN dependency. Discovery R11, signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis, was +0.790 with a 95% interval [0.760, 0.820]. Independent validation R26 was +0.797 with an independent interval [0.744, 0.850] under stricter validation-adjusted coverage. Both lower bounds are far above any approximate 10% clinically relevant threshold on the WRN dependency score scale, and the two estimates are highly consistent. I therefore accept H11 as a robust dataset-specific association and close its direct investigation because the central direct claim has now been internally validated. This does not establish causality in cells or generalizable clinical utility; it establishes that the supplied data and supplied independent validation both show a large MSI-high versus WRN dependency-score difference.

With H11 replicated, the strongest evidence in the project remains the trio of large dependency-score associations: MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency (H11, replicated; H25 adenocarcinoma-restricted), SMARCA4-loss cells show stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12; H26 adenocarcinoma-restricted), and KEAP1-loss cells show weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13; H27 adenocarcinoma-restricted). The first of these is now the most secure claim in the accepted set. The current context results are mostly reassuring but incomplete. Lineage-subtype interaction tests suggest no strong evidence of SMARCA4-loss effect modification by subtype (H15 rejected), while WRN and NFE2L2 subtype interactions remain imprecise but low priority. Library ky context tests showed no meaningful WRN interaction (H28 rejected) and an imprecise near-null NFE2L2 interaction (H30 deferred); the SMARCA2 ky interaction is borderline and unresolved (H29), so the newly registered direct ky subgroup test H36 is important. Adherent-culture interactions are pending, and I registered direct adherent-subgroup mean differences for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss because these will provide interpretable within-culture effect sizes rather than only interaction contrasts.

Negative findings remain important: KRAS mutation on BRAF dependency, BRAF V600E on BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification on STAT3 dependency, the original KEAP1-loss stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis, MYC amplification on POLR2A dependency, the SMARCA4-loss by subtype interaction, and the MSI-high by ky library interaction for WRN were rejected as not supporting clinically meaningful effects in their registered directions. Unresolved uncertainty remains for direct KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2/TP53/MYC associations, the EGFR/KRAS-wild-type subgroup interaction, low-priority library and subtype interactions, ARID1A-loss on SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss on USP7, and the pending context analyses. The most informative next analyses are the direct ky tests H36-H38, the new direct adherent tests, and then the marker/context tests. If the context tests remain broadly consistent, the next independent validation should prioritize H12, because it is a large mechanistically meaningful association without independent replication; H13 would be the next candidate. If a context test shows strong attenuation or heterogeneity, that should be investigated before spending additional validation on that pathway.

Registered new mechanistically motivated comparisons targeting outcome–predictor pairs not yet explored, while retaining the accepted WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss findings for follow-up context checks. The new RIT1 panel tests upstream RTK-to-RAS/MAPK signaling logic: KRAS and BRAF mutant cells are hypothesized to be less dependent on upstream RIT1, so their dependency scores should be less negative than in wild-type cells (positive raw difference), whereas ERBB2 or EGFR amplification could reflect receptor-driven signaling that still uses RIT1 and thus could be associated with stronger RIT1 dependency (more negative scores). The EGFR/RIT1 direction is deliberately uncertain because the direct EGFR/dependency_EGFR claim was not externally consistent, but testing RIT1 asks a distinct mechanistic question. MYC amplification versus dependency_DHX9 tests whether transcription-factor amplification creates a helicase/transcription-stress dependency beyond the null MYC/POLR2A result. TP53 loss versus dependency_RPL11 and dependency_USP7 extends p53-pathway dependency logic: TP53 loss should reduce reliance on p53-pathway nodes, giving less negative scores. The MDM2 interaction refinement asks whether the weak TP53-loss effect is modified by MTAP loss, a co-deleted p53-region alteration that could alter MDM2-pathway context. Finally, EGFR amplification versus TMED10 probes whether RTK-amplified cells are more dependent on secretory-pathway cargo trafficking. These proposals improve broad coverage of the untested dependency scores and provide falsifiable alternatives to the current accepted synthetic-lethal associations. The next analysis phase should prioritize these new tests together with the highest-value pending context tests: direct ky-library SMARCA2 dependency and direct adherent-culture tests for the accepted associations. Marker D/E/F tests and lower-priority KRAS subtype/culture interactions can be deferred unless they become mechanistically or robustness-priority based on results. All claims remain dataset-specific associations; validation will be used to distinguish replication from incidental dataset structure.

Selected twelve existing analyses that split between robustness follow-up of the accepted dependency associations and new mechanistic broad-exploration tests. First, I prioritize direct within-context mean differences for the three large accepted associations in Ky library and adherent culture contexts: H36 for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 in Ky, H37 for MSI-high/WRN in Ky, H38 for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 in Ky, and H39-H41 for the same predictors in adherent culture. These are more interpretable than interaction contrasts and are needed because the Ky interaction for SMARCA2/H29 was borderline while the WRN and NFE2L2 Ky interactions were imprecise but not supportive. Direct adherent tests assess whether the accepted effects persist in the dominant culture context rather than only in the full eligible sample. Second, I run six untested mechanistic comparisons: H42-H44 test RTK-to-RAS/MAPK signaling logic around RIT1 dependency under KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification; H46 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger DHX9 dependency, a plausible transcription-stress/helicase relationship distinct from the null MYC/POLR2A result; and H47-H48 test whether TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency on p53-pathway components RPL11 and USP7. I do not run arbitrary research-marker tests or the MDM2/MTAP interaction because their prior mechanistic specificity is lower and existing unresolved claims are already low priority. I also defer EGFR/RIT1 and TMED10 tests because the EGFR-dependency signals have been inconsistent and these hypotheses are more speculative.

The new direct context tests strongly support the three previously accepted dependency associations. For SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 within the Ky library, R27 is signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis and is +0.814 with a 95% interval [0.774, 0.855]. This is far above a conservative ~10% score-scale benchmark and resolves the earlier borderline Ky interaction by showing that the main SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect remains very large inside Ky cells. For MSI-high versus dependency_WRN within Ky, R28 is +0.751 [0.693, 0.809]; although the exposed Ky/MSI-high cell has only 27 observations, the lower bound remains enormous, so I accept it as a dataset-specific context association while noting small-cell caution. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency within Ky, R29 is +0.787 [0.741, 0.832]. The adherent-culture direct tests are similarly strong: WRN/MSI-high +0.816 [0.784, 0.849], SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss +0.786 [0.762, 0.810], and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss +0.795 [0.770, 0.820]. I accept H36-H41 as dataset-specific within-context associations supporting the robustness of the accepted trio, not as independent validation.

The most important new mechanistic result is TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7. With direction +1, a positive signed estimate means TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency. R38 is +0.804 [0.783, 0.825], an extremely large and precise dataset-specific association. It is mechanistically plausible because USP7 functions in p53/MDM2-related regulation, and TP53 loss could reduce reliance on USP7; however, this remains only an association in the supplied data. I accept H48 and keep it active, with context follow-up proposed before deciding whether it should become a leading validated claim.

The other new mechanistic tests are mostly null or imprecise. KRAS mutation versus dependency_RIT1, R33, is +0.003 with interval [-0.016, 0.023]; the upper bound is below the approximate 10% RIT1 score-scale benchmark, so I reject H42. BRAF V600E versus RIT1, R34, and ERBB2 amplification versus RIT1, R35, are near zero but have wide intervals that touch borderline clinically meaningful values in their claimed directions; H43 and H44 remain unresolved but deferred because the point estimates are negligible and the RIT1 panel otherwise gives little support. MYC amplification versus DHX9, R36, is near null with a borderline negative lower bound, so H46 is unresolved but deferred. TP53 loss versus RPL11, R37, is also near null with a borderline positive upper bound, so H47 is unresolved but deferred.

I request independent validation for H12. The central SMARCA4-loss/dependency_SMARCA2 association is large in the full eligible sample and now shows very large direct effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky, and adherent contexts; external validation would distinguish robust replication from shared same-dataset structure or correlated genomic confounding. H48 is the next validation candidate after its context tests, and H13 would remain a later candidate. All conclusions remain associations in this dataset; unadjusted Welch comparisons can be confounded by correlated alterations, multiple testing is present, and no causal or broadly generalizable claim is made.

The new validation decisively strengthens H12 and disposes of the unresolved H4. For H12, SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, discovery R12 was +0.782 [0.761, 0.802], signed to the hypothesis that SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger, more negative SMARCA2 dependency. Independent validation R39 was +0.805 [0.775, 0.836] under the stricter validation-adjusted interval. The lower bounds are far above any reasonable approximate 10% effect benchmark on the SMARCA2 score scale, and discovery and validation magnitudes are highly consistent. Therefore H12 is accepted as an independently replicated dataset-specific association, not as a causal or clinical claim. The previously accepted within-context confirmations H26 adenocarcinoma, H36 Ky library, and H40 adherent culture are now treated as completed robustness checks and closed. The borderline Ky interaction H29 also is closed as an investigation line because the central effect is validated and very large in Ky itself, although the interaction estimate remains statistically imprecise and unresolved in a strict sense.

For H4, EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR, the response-deadline validation is negative for the registered hypothesis. Discovery R4 was only weakly positive in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, +0.029 [0.001, 0.057], and validation R13 was -0.013 [-0.059, 0.033], crossing zero and pointing in the opposite signed direction. There is no stable evidence for a clinically meaningful EGFR-amplification association with EGFR dependency. I therefore reject H4 and close it. This is an important negative control against overinterpreting small near-threshold discovery estimates.

The current supported core findings are: MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency, replicated in H11 and context-supported in H25/H37/H39; SMARCA4-loss cells show stronger SMARCA2 dependency, now replicated in H12 and context-supported in H26/H36/H40; KEAP1-loss cells show weaker NFE2L2 dependency in H13, H27, H38, and H41, but this major association has not yet received independent validation; and TP53-loss cells show weaker USP7 dependency in H48, with a very large discovery estimate +0.804 [0.783, 0.825], also not yet validated. Negative or rejected findings include KRAS mutation on BRAF dependency, BRAF V600E on BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification on STAT3 and EGFR dependency, the original KEAP1-loss stronger-NFE2L2 direction, MYC amplification on POLR2A dependency, the SMARCA4-loss lineage-subtype interaction, the MSI-high Ky-library interaction, and KRAS mutation on RIT1 dependency. Unresolved low-priority uncertainty remains for small direct EGFR, ERBB2, TP53-MDM2, MYC-USP7, marker-modifier, and some interaction contrasts.

The most informative next analyses are the TP53-loss/USP7 context tests H51-H54, followed by marker-modifier tests for the accepted effects H17-H23, and broad KIF18A tests H55-H56. If TP53-loss/USP7 remains large and consistent across adenocarcinoma, Ky, adherent, and MTAP-loss contexts, H48 should become the next independent validation target; if it is context-specific or attenuated, investigate the context before validation. H13 remains a later validation candidate. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset and supplied validation splits, not causal effects or guaranteed generalizable findings.

The next highest-value exploration is to resolve whether the very large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust and whether it is confounded or modified by MTAP loss, a common co-deleted 9p alteration near CDKN2A/p53-related biology. I therefore registered a direct USP7 context test within MTAP-loss cells, a direct MTAP-loss effect on USP7, and a direct MTAP-loss effect on MDM2. If the USP7 association is stable across TP53-loss contexts and is not merely tracking MTAP co-loss, H48 should become the next independent validation target. I also registered downstream RAS/MAPK cross-dependency tests: KRAS or BRAF alterations may reduce dependence on upstream EGFR or KRAS itself, and KRAS mutation may reduce dependence on ERBB2. These are distinct from the earlier rejected EGFR-amplification results and test pathway position rather than receptor amplification. ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 and TMED10 tests receptor-driven signaling dependencies beyond EGFR amplification. Finally, I registered TP53-loss versus POLR2A and DHX9 to ask whether p53 loss changes transcription-stress or helicase/R-loop dependencies, and a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 context test within ARID1A-loss cells because ARID1A loss may modify chromatin-remodeler dependencies even though the direct ARID1A effect was null. These proposals preserve the current validation plan: first confirm H48 contexts, then request independent validation for H48 if consistent; H13 remains the next major unvalidated candidate after that.

I am using this analysis block primarily to determine whether the large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association (H48/R38) is robust enough to become the next independent-validation target and whether it could be confounded or modified by MTAP-loss co-deletion. Therefore I run the direct context effects H51 (adenocarcinoma), H52 (Ky library), and H53 (adherent culture), the MTAP-loss subgroup direct effect H57, and the MTAP-loss interaction H54 for dependency_USP7. I also request direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2 (H58 and H59) because MTAP deletion is biologically and genomically plausible as a confounder or modifier of p53-pathway dependency relationships. If H48 remains large across contexts and MTAP direct effects do not dominate, I will likely request independent validation of H48 in appraisal. The remaining six analyses provide scientifically informative breadth and specificity checks: H66 tests whether the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association persists within ARID1A-loss cells; H55 and H56 begin broad coverage of untested KIF18A dependency under MYC amplification and TP53 loss; and H65 and H67 test whether TP53 loss has broader p53-associated effects on transcription-stress/helicase nodes POLR2A and DHX9, helping distinguish a selective USP7 effect from a general p53-loss signature. I defer the newly registered EGFR/KRAS downstream tests and TMED10/ERBB2 tests for now because the EGFR-dependency line has already failed validation and the TMED10/ERBB2 hypothesis is more speculative.

The new TP53-loss/USP7 context tests strongly support the central accepted association and justify independent validation of the full-sample claim H48. The signed direction is +1 for TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and all four direct context effects are large and precise: adenocarcinoma R40 is +0.803 [0.778, 0.827], Ky library R41 is +0.769 [0.727, 0.812], adherent culture R42 is +0.803 [0.779, 0.827], and MTAP-loss cells R44 is +0.758 [0.709, 0.808]. These are far above any conservative approximate 10% effect benchmark on the dependency-score scale, and the MTAP-loss subgroup lower bound remains very large despite only 69 exposed observations. I therefore accept H51, H52, H53, and H57 as dataset-specific context support and close them as completed robustness checks for H48.

The MTAP-loss interaction H54 is a useful confounding check but does not support the registered positive interaction. R43 is negative, -0.056 [-0.111, -0.002], indicating a small attenuation of the TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association in MTAP-loss cells rather than enhancement. Because the main effect remains large within MTAP-loss cells and the interaction magnitude is small relative to the main ~0.76-0.80 effects, I reject H54 as an enhanced MTAP-loss modification claim and close it. Direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2, R45 and R46, are near null and imprecise; H58 and H59 remain unresolved but deferred. They do not show that MTAP loss alone is a dominant driver strong enough to invalidate H48, though correlated 9p co-deletion remains a caution when interpreting this association.

H66 adds a second robustness check for the already independently validated SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association: within ARID1A-loss cells, SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, R47 is +0.805 [0.755, 0.854]. I accept H66 and close it as a completed context check; it does not require separate validation because H12 is already validated.

The p53-specificity checks are informative. H65 is null/near-null for TP53 loss versus weaker POLR2A dependency: R50 is -0.014 [-0.035, 0.007], and the upper bound is well below a rough clinical benchmark, so I reject the positive POLR2A hypothesis. H67 also does not support the registered stronger DHX9 direction; R51 is negative, -0.024 [-0.044, -0.004], indicating a small opposite direction rather than the claimed association. I reject H67 for the registered hypothesis. Together, these results make the TP53-loss/USP7 association look more selective than a broad p53-loss effect on transcription or helicase dependencies, although residual specificity uncertainty remains.

The KIF18A tests remain near-null but are not fully conclusive for small clinically meaningful effects: H55 MYC amplification R48 is +0.009 [-0.015, 0.032], and H56 TP53 loss R49 is +0.019 [-0.002, 0.041]. I leave H55 and H56 unresolved and deferred because point estimates are small, intervals include zero, and the upper tails may touch a borderline benchmark; these are low priority relative to H48 validation. Overall, the evidence now supports requesting independent validation for H48. This would test whether the large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust beyond the discovery partition and correlated same-dataset structure. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or generalized clinical claims.

The delivered validation resolves both pending deadlines. For H11, MSI-high versus dependency_WRN, the independent validation R26 is +0.797 with lower bound 0.744, while discovery R11 was +0.790 with lower bound 0.760. The direction, magnitude, and practical significance are highly consistent, and both lower bounds are far above any conservative approximate 10% dependency-score benchmark. I therefore keep H11 accepted and close it as an independently replicated dataset-specific association: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency in this supplied dataset. For H48, TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, validation R52 is +0.7995 with lower bound 0.768, closely matching discovery R38 +0.804 [0.783,0.825] and the large direct context effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky library, adherent culture, and MTAP-loss cells. I accept H48 and close its investigation as robust within the supplied discovery/validation structure. This is not causal evidence, but it is now one of the strongest supported associations: TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. The MTAP-loss checks do not invalidate it: direct MTAP effects were near null, and the MTAP-loss interaction was a small attenuation, not an enhancement, of the TP53 loss effect. The p53 specificity checks also make the USP7 association look relatively selective: TP53 loss was not meaningfully associated with the registered POLR2A hypothesis and did not support the registered stronger DHX9 hypothesis. 

The independently replicated core now includes H11, H12, and H48. The largest remaining unvalidated accepted effect is H13, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. It is supported by a very large discovery estimate and multiple context-specific confirmations, but it still needs independent validation. I therefore reopened H13 as active and closed the context-specific NFE2L2 confirmations as completed robustness checks. Next analyses should prioritize independent validation of H13, while also running the registered marker modifier tests H17-H23. The new proposals add biologically motivated follow-up: whether STK11 loss modifies the KEAP1/NFE2L2 or MSI/WRN associations, whether ARID1A loss modifies the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 interaction, whether BRCA2 loss increases DHX9 or POLR2A dependency, and whether CDKN2A loss or PTEN loss produce p53- or USP7-related dependency shifts that might indicate broader pathway co-occurrence effects. Negative findings remain important: EGFR amplification failed independent validation for EGFR dependency; KRAS/BRAF/RIT1/ERBB2 contrasts were mostly near null; several MTAP and marker interactions are unresolved but low priority; and constructed markers D/E/F still lack clear interpretation beyond assay controls. All accepted claims remain dataset-specific associations, not causal effects or guaranteed generalizable clinical claims.

The current strongest validated dataset-specific effects are MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency. The next highest-priority scientific target is independent validation of KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, but at the explore stage I am registering additional falsifiable comparisons that either broaden pathway coverage or provide specificity/confounding checks around the accepted and near-accepted effects.

First, I registered PIK3CA-mutation effects on STAT3, EGFR, and ERBB2. PIK3CA activating mutations constitutively activate downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. This could increase STAT3 dependency through kinase-signaling crosstalk, so I proposed PIK3CA versus stronger STAT3 dependency under direction -1. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, PIK3CA-mutant cells could have weaker dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; I therefore proposed positive mean differences for EGFR and ERBB2, meaning less negative dependency scores and therefore weaker dependency. The alternative is null because STAT3 may be largely independent of PIK3CA, or because receptor-dependency relationships are lineage and mutation-context dependent.

Second, I registered NF1-loss effects on STAT3 and KRAS. NF1 is a RAS-GTPase-activating protein, so NF1 loss should produce elevated RAS-MAPK activity. A plausible hypothesis is that NF1-loss tumors are more dependent on STAT3, a stress-signaling node downstream of inflammatory and growth-factor pathways, so the registered STAT3 claim expects stronger, more negative dependency. For KRAS, NF1 loss could increase addiction to KRAS-GTP signaling, but it could also make KRAS less selectively required because other RAS isoforms or downstream effectors compensate; I still registered stronger KRAS dependency as a falsifiable hypothesis but will treat any negative or small estimate as informative against the simple NF1-loss-to-KRAS-dependence model.

Third, I registered a receptor-crosstalk comparison: ERBB2 amplification versus EGFR dependency. EGFR and ERBB2 form heterodimers and share downstream signaling. ERBB2 amplification could compensate for EGFR, producing weaker EGFR dependency, which is the positive raw exposed-minus-comparator hypothesis. Alternatively, ERBB2-amplified cells might retain or co-select EGFR pathway dependence, producing a negative raw contrast. This comparison adds a new receptor-dependency relationship rather than repeating the failed EGFR-amplification direct dependency line.

Fourth, I registered BRCA2-loss versus KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 loss creates homologous-recombination deficiency and genome instability. KIF18A is mitotic and often exposed by replication-stress or mitotic checkpoint defects. A stronger, more negative KIF18A dependency would be consistent with BRCA2-deficient cells being more vulnerable to mitotic spindle control loss. The alternative is specificity: BRCA2 may alter DNA repair dependencies such as DHX9 or POLR2A without changing KIF18A.

Fifth, I registered MSI-high versus DHX9 dependency. MSI-high is already associated with a very large WRN-dependency effect in this dataset. Testing MSI-high against DHX9 asks whether MSI broadly increases dependency on DNA/R-loop-associated helicase nodes or whether the MSI association is relatively WRN-selective. The registered direction is stronger DHX9 dependency with MSI-high, but a null result would support WRN specificity and would not invalidate the validated MSI/WRN association.

Sixth, I registered modification checks using CDKN2A loss. CDKN2A co-deletion or pathway alteration is a natural confounding context for the TP53-loss/USP7 association and also biologically relevant to MDM2. The interaction claims test whether the TP53-loss contrast differs in CDKN2A-loss versus non-loss cells. A positive interaction for USP7 would mean the TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 contrast is even larger in CDKN2A-loss cells; a negative interaction would mean attenuation. Direct CDKN2A-loss versus USP7 is also registered because if CDKN2A loss alone is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, the TP53-loss USP7 association may partly reflect broader p53- or cell-cycle-pathway co-alteration rather than a uniquely TP53-loss-specific association. These are context and specificity checks, not reasons to discard H48 unless they reveal a dominant direct or interaction effect.

Finally, I registered a KEAP1-loss-by-MYC-amplification interaction for dependency_NFE2L2. KEAP1 loss is currently accepted as associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and the interaction asks whether MYC amplification changes that relationship. MYC amplification may increase oxidative and metabolic stress, potentially changing NRF2-pathway dependencies. This is biologically motivated and directly related to the major unvalidated candidate H13, although independent validation of H13 remains the next central priority. All new comparisons are treated as dataset-specific associations; none should be interpreted as causal or generally clinically actionable unless further evidence and independent validation support it.

There are no assessments_due, so I do not change any existing claim conclusions in this form. The scientific priority is to build same-dataset robustness and specificity evidence around the strongest accepted effects before requesting independent validation. The independently replicated core is H11, H12, and H48. The largest accepted but unvalidated effect remains H13, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, so I am selecting tests that either test context independence, assay-marker robustness, or biological modifiers for H11/H12/H13 rather than running already tested comparisons. I selected six constructed-marker tests: H17-H19 and H21-H23. These ask whether the MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations persist in marker-positive strata, and whether markers D/E/F have any main association with the corresponding dependencies. Because the markers are constructed assays without assigned biological role, I expect near-null marker main effects and near-null interactions; if interactions or direct effects are small, they support assay robustness but I would not interpret them as biologically meaningful unless they are large and precisely estimated. I selected H31-H33 as culture_type modifier checks for the three central dependencies. These are technical context checks for the validated WRN and SMARCA2 effects and the accepted NFE2L2 effect. Since adherent culture is the majority, these may be modestly powered but are useful for detecting gross environment-driven artifacts. If the interactions are small or intervals are wide, the main effects remain accepted; if a large interaction appears, the affected main claim should be narrowed. I selected H69-H71 for STK11-related biology: direct STK11 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency, KEAP1-loss interaction with STK11 loss for NFE2L2, and MSI-high interaction with STK11 loss for WRN. STK11 loss is common in lung adenocarcinoma and biologically connected to lung cancer stress biology and co-occurrence patterns with KEAP1/NFE2L2. These tests refine whether H13 or H11 are merely tracking STK11 co-alteration or whether they remain independent associations. All results will be interpreted as dataset-specific associations, not causal or general clinical claims, and acceptance will require evidence of scientifically meaningful magnitude, ideally with interval bounds consistent with the 10% threshold. New broad pathway follow-ups, CDKN2A/USP7 checks, BRCA2 tests, and PIK3CA/NF1/ERBB2 pathway contrasts remain active for later if these robustness and modifier results leave specific questions unresolved.

The new evidence mostly provides negative specificity and context checks around the central accepted effects. For the constructed markers, H17/R53, H18/R54, H19/R55, H21/R56, H22/R57, and H23/R58 are all small and imprecise. Their signed estimates are near zero, and the 95% upper bounds are roughly 0.028-0.060, below the approximate 0.1 dependency-score benchmark I am using to distinguish trivial from scientifically meaningful associations. These nulls do not create scientific claims; they instead suggest that the large WRN/SMARCA2/NFE2L2 associations are not tracking arbitrary marker-positive groups. I therefore reject the registered marker main-effect and marker-interaction claims as completed negative controls and close them. 

The culture interaction results are mixed but mostly reassuring. H32/R60 for SMARCA2 and H33/R61 for NFE2L2 are null, with upper bounds 0.0596 and 0.0391, below the practical benchmark; I reject those as meaningful modifiers of the validated SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and accepted KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 relationships. H31/R59 for MSI-high/WRN is the only borderline culture result: the signed interaction is +0.114 with 95% interval [0.041, 0.187]. The point estimate is above the benchmark, but the lower bound is below it, so I leave H31 unresolved and deferred rather than accepting a clinically meaningful culture modification. Importantly, this borderline interaction does not invalidate the independently validated H11 MSI-high/WRN association, because the adherent-culture main effect remains extremely large at R30 = +0.816 [0.784, 0.849]. 

The STK11 checks also support specificity of the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 relationship. H69/R62 tests whether STK11 loss modifies the KEAP1-loss contrast; the signed estimate is -0.029 [-0.088, 0.030], so the upper bound is well below the benchmark and the registered direction is unsupported. H70/R63 tests STK11 loss alone against NFE2L2 dependency; the signed estimate is -0.023 [-0.065, 0.018], again null. I reject H69 and H70 as completed checks and close them. The MSI-high/STK11 interaction H71/R64 is uninformative because the MSI-high and STK11-loss interaction cell has only 19 observations and the Welch analysis is invalid. I leave H71 unresolved but close it because this exact stratification is underpowered and future effort should go to independent validation of H13. 

I am requesting independent validation for H13, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is the largest accepted but unvalidated effect. The main discovery association is R7 = +0.797 [0.776, 0.819], and it is supported by context effects in adenocarcinoma R16 = +0.795, Ky library R29 = +0.787, and adherent culture R32 = +0.795. The new robustness checks reduce concern that the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is explained by marker-D assay artifacts, culture environment, or STK11 co-alteration: marker D direct and interaction effects are null, culture interaction is null, and STK11 direct and interaction effects are null. This does not establish causality or clinical generalizability, but it makes H13 the best next candidate for independent validation. All accepted associations remain dataset-specific statistical associations. 

From a critical-reviewer perspective, the main threats are multiplicity and correlated genomic co-alterations. I am not accepting the borderline H31 culture interaction because its interval includes clinically trivial effects, and I am treating marker D/E/F tests as arbitrary-assay controls rather than biological pathways. The central validated claims H11, H12, and H48 remain distinct from the exploratory negative controls.

The delivered validation resolves the two due claims and completes the main independent-validation stage for the strongest associations. For H12, the independent validation R39 is signed +0.805 [0.775, 0.836] for the hypothesis that SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency, closely matching discovery R12 at +0.782 [0.761, 0.802]. Because the lower bound is far above any reasonable 10-percent practical benchmark and the direction and magnitude are replicated, I keep H12 accepted and close it as a dataset-specific association: SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency in this supplied dataset. For H13, the independent validation R65 is signed +0.804 [0.773, 0.835] for the refined hypothesis that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, closely matching discovery R7 at +0.797 [0.776, 0.819]. This is very large and precisely estimated, so I accept and close H13. The signed direction means the raw KEAP1-loss minus KEAP1-non-loss difference is positive, i.e. less negative NFE2L2 scores and therefore weaker dependency. The opposite claim H7 is now explicitly rejected because the same validation strongly contradicts stronger NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells.

The supported core now consists of four independently replicated dataset-specific associations: MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency (H11), SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency (H48), and KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13). Each has discovery and validation estimates near 0.8 with lower bounds well above the practical benchmark. Context-specific confirmations and null modifier checks reduce concern that these are simple artifacts of lineage, CRISPR library, culture, constructed marker assays, or tested co-alterations. For H13, adenocarcinoma, Ky-library, and adherent-culture direct effects are large and positive, whereas marker D, culture-interaction, and STK11 direct/interaction tests are null. For H48, context effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky-library, adherent culture, and MTAP-loss cells remain large; direct MTAP effects and MTAP-by-TP53 interaction do not support a dominant co-deletion explanation, although correlated 9p biology remains a caution.

Negative and low-priority findings are scientifically useful. EGFR amplification did not replicate as a clinically meaningful dependency association in EGFR dependency (H4 failed validation). KRAS-mutation contrasts for KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, and RIT1 dependencies are mostly near null or imprecise. Many small effects involving MYC amplification, TP53 loss, MTAP loss, p53-pathway co-alterations, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, and receptor pathway markers remain below the practical benchmark or unresolved and should not be accepted. Constructed markers D/E/F behaved as null controls and should not be interpreted as biological pathways. The STK11 checks for NFE2L2 and KEAP1 were null; the MSI-high STK11 interaction was underpowered. The only borderline context modifier is H31, where the adherent-culture interaction for MSI-high versus WRN dependency is +0.114 [0.041, 0.187]. Its point estimate crosses the practical benchmark, but its lower bound does not, so it remains unresolved and does not overturn H11, whose main and adherent-culture effects remain enormous.

Unresolved uncertainty is mainly residual confounding by correlated genomic alterations, underpowered subgroup interactions, and lack of causal or external-generalizability evidence. These results establish associations in the supplied dataset/validation structure, not mechanisms of dependency, not necessarily causal driver relationships, and not guaranteed clinical biomarker claims.

The most informative next analysis is to test specificity and modifiers of the validated core rather than pursue near-null small main effects. I prioritize the already active CDKN2A checks around p53 biology (H85/H86/H88), BRCA2/MSI DNA-repair selectivity tests (H73/H74/H83/H84), MYC amplification modification of the KEAP1-loss effect (H87), and receptor/PI3K/NF1 crosstalk tests (H77-H82). I also register two negative-control comparisons: KEAP1 loss versus WRN dependency and KEAP1 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency. These are expected to be null if the KEAP1 association is NFE2L2-selective; a large effect would indicate a broader dependency pattern and would require reevaluation of specificity.

There are no assessments_due at this explore stage, so I am not changing existing scientific conclusions. The accepted validated core is MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The next useful comparisons should test whether these large associations are biologically specific, robust to CRISPR-screen quality, and not explained by common co-alterations or pathway bypass contexts.  

I registered co-alteration refinements for the two most important non-MRE pathway dependencies: TP53-loss by SMARCA4-loss for USP7 dependency, and KEAP1-loss by TP53-loss for NFE2L2 dependency. These ask whether the main dependency contrast is enlarged or attenuated in a relevant co-altered tumor-suppressor context. A large attenuation would suggest that correlated losses confound the main association; a large enhancement would define a context where the dependency is especially strong. Because I expect independence more than a strong interaction, the anticipated direction is uncertain, and I will only accept a meaningful interaction if the signed effect is large and the interval remains above the practical dependency benchmark.  

I registered PI3K/RAS/receptor crosstalk checks: PIK3CA mutation effects on EGFR dependency modified by KRAS mutation, and ERBB2 amplification effects on ERBB2 dependency modified by PIK3CA mutation. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, receptor-dependency differences should be smaller in PIK3CA-mutant cells, giving a negative interaction. Conversely, if receptor pathway activation remains required, estimates will be near zero or positive. These comparisons broaden beyond the earlier EGFR-amplification line, which failed validation, and test pathway redundancy in a falsifiable way.  

I registered CRISPR-activity robustness interactions using high Cas9 activity, cas9_activity_pct >= 75%, for each core association: MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2. Cas9 activity is a measured technical predictor, so a dependency association that depends only on high-Cas9 cells would be more screen-quality driven, whereas an association similar across high and lower Cas9 strata would be more robust. I expect null or small interactions, and these should not replace the central main effects unless they are large and consistently signed.  

Finally, I registered direct STK11-loss versus WRN and SMARCA2 dependencies as specificity controls. STK11 loss was previously null for the KEAP1/NFE2L2 contrast, but direct tests against WRN and SMARCA2 clarify whether STK11 co-alteration is broadly associated with these validated dependencies. I expect null effects; large effects would indicate broader lung cancer context dependence and would require revisiting the specificity of the main effects. All proposals are same-dataset association tests and will be interpreted as dataset-specific associations, not causal mechanisms or guaranteed clinical biomarkers.

There are no assessments due, so no claim status changes are made. The analysis budget is allocated to discovery tests that directly interrogate the four already validated dataset-specific associations rather than expanding many low-priority main effects. H95-H98 test whether the MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 contrasts are robust to high Cas9 activity, a measured screen-quality predictor. These interactions are expected to be small if the core effects are not artifacts of CRISPR-screen performance; large signed effects would require narrowing the corresponding main associations to Cas9-quality strata. I assess all newly delivered discovery results. All 12 new estimates are small relative to the validated core effects and do not provide evidence of a clinically meaningful association at the approximate 0.1 dependency-score benchmark. The high-Cas9 interaction tests H95-H98 are particularly useful technical checks: H95/R66 is +0.023 [-0.043, 0.090], H96/R67 +0.018 [-0.028, 0.065], H97/R68 -0.002 [-0.049, 0.045], and H98/R69 -0.007 [-0.057, 0.043]. These intervals include zero and are bounded below the practical benchmark, so they do not support the idea that the MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, or KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations exist only in high-Cas9 screens. I reject these interaction claims and close them as completed robustness checks.

The specificity controls also remain null. H89/R70 tests KEAP1 loss against WRN dependency, +0.002 [-0.034, 0.030], and H90/R71 tests KEAP1 loss against SMARCA2 dependency, +0.009 [-0.033, 0.052]. These nulls reduce concern that KEAP1 loss is a broad nonselective modifier of these validated dependencies and are compatible with NFE2L2-selective specificity. H84/R76 tests MSI-high against DHX9 dependency, signed estimate +0.020 [-0.017, 0.056], which is far weaker than the validated MSI-high/WRN association (~0.8) and does not support a broad DNA-repair or nucleic-acid metabolism dependency effect. H87/R77 tests MYC-amplification modification of KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2, -0.006 [-0.072, 0.061], and does not support a MYC-dependent alteration of the KEAP1 association.

The co-alteration checks similarly do not reveal dominant confounding. H85/R72 tests TP53-loss modification by CDKN2A loss for USP7, +0.011 [-0.038, 0.060]; H88/R73 tests CDKN2A loss main effect on USP7, +0.004 [-0.039, 0.048]; H91/R74 tests TP53-loss modification by SMARCA4 loss for USP7, +0.022 [-0.026, 0.071]. H92/R75 tests KEAP1-loss modification by TP53 loss for NFE2L2, +0.039 [-0.016, 0.095]; the point estimate is positive and near but below 0.1, with lower bound negative, so it is not accepted as a meaningful context effect and is rejected as a completed check.

From a multiplicity and critical-review perspective, these results are reassuring because they are mostly null after many exploratory stratifications, and the four central associations remain the only effects with effects near 0.8 and tight intervals. The new evidence does not justify accepting a new modifier or creating new context-specific claims. Therefore I close all 12 new due claims as rejected. 

The only active scientific uncertainty that could benefit from validation is H31, the MSI-high/WRN interaction with adherent culture. Its discovery estimate is +0.114 [0.041, 0.187], so the point estimate exceeds the practical benchmark but the interval remains compatible with clinically trivial effects. Validating H31 directly tests whether the independently replicated MSI-high/WRN association is meaningfully modified by culture context. I keep H31 unresolved and active, and request independent validation for H31. The new Cas9, KEAP1-specificity, co-alteration, MYC, and DHX9 checks do not themselves warrant validation because their intervals exclude clinically meaningful effects.

The delivered validations require explicit reassessment. H48 reached its validation deadline: independent validation R52 is signed +0.799 with lower bound +0.768 and upper bound +0.831, closely matching discovery R38 at +0.804 with lower bound +0.783 and upper bound +0.825. Because the signed hypothesis direction is +1, the raw contrast is positive, meaning TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. I keep H48 accepted and closed. H31 failed validation: discovery R59 suggested an adherent-culture interaction for MSI-high WRN dependency, signed +0.114 with 95 percent interval +0.041 to +0.187; independent validation R78 is only +0.0236 with interval -0.0865 to +0.1338, spanning zero, clinically trivial, and opposite directions. I reject H31 and close it as unsupported context modification, while preserving H11 and H39 main effects. H55 also fails validation: discovery R48 +0.0090 and validation R79 +0.0126 are near zero; I reject it. The independently supported core remains: H11 MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency; H12 SMARCA4-loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency; H48 TP53-loss -> weaker USP7 dependency; H13 KEAP1-loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Each has discovery and validation estimates near 0.80 with lower bounds far above the practical absolute benchmark and far above any plausible 10 percent threshold in arbitrary dependency units. Subgroup analyses in adenocarcinoma, Ky library, adherent culture, and ARID1A-loss contexts remain large where tested, whereas Cas9-high, library, lineage, culture, marker D/E/F, and most co-alteration interactions are small. I additionally closed a batch of completed negative same-dataset checks because their point estimates are small, intervals include zero, and validation is not warranted: H1 KRAS mutation vs KRAS dependency, H6 ERBB2 amplification vs ERBB2 dependency, H43 and H44 RIT1 pathway checks, H10 H46 and H55 MYC-amplification checks, H56 and H47 TP53-loss checks on KIF18A and RPL11, H58 and H59 MTAP-loss p53 co-alteration checks, H34 ARID1A direct chromatin control, H35 KEAP1-to-USP7 cross-check, and H14 H16 H20 H29 H30 context interactions. These negative findings are useful because they show the core associations are not explained by broad receptor, MYC, MTAP, ARID1A, constructed-marker, or most technical/context effects. Unresolved scientific uncertainty remains for active no-evidence specificity and pathway tests, especially direct STK11-loss on WRN and SMARCA2 H99 and H100, BRCA2-loss on DHX9 POLR2A and KIF18A H73 H74 and H83, PIK3CA NF1 and ERBB2 crosstalk H77 through H82 and H93 and H94, MDM2 co-alteration checks H75 H86 and H50, and ARID1A interaction H72. These results are associations in the supplied dataset and validation splits, not causal driver relationships or externally generalizable clinical biomarkers.

There are no assessments due at this explore stage, so no existing claim is being reassessed now. The accepted, independently replicated dataset-specific core remains: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H11); SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12); TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency (H48); and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13). Each accepted core effect has discovery and validation estimates near 0.8 in signed form, with lower bounds far above the practical absolute dependency-score benchmark and far above any plausible 10-percent interpretation in arbitrary units. The scientific question is now less about whether these associations exist in the supplied dataset and more about how specific, robust, and context-limited they are.

The first proposed refinements ask whether two core associations persist in high-Cas9 screens, a measured screen-quality stratum. The WRN MSI-high comparison and the USP7 TP53-loss comparison are tested directly among screens with cas9_activity_pct >= 75%. Expected directions are the same as the overall core claims: MSI-high should show more negative WRN scores, and TP53-loss should show less negative USP7 scores. Large, precisely estimated effects in this stratum would support robustness against Cas9-performance dependence. Small or attenuated effects would be important because they would indicate that the high-level interactions previously tested were not sufficient to rule out a quality-dependent context restriction. I will accept only effects whose intervals remain clearly above the practical ~0.1 dependency-score benchmark.

The next set is a specificity battery for the large WRN and SMARCA2 dependencies. BRCA2 loss and TP53 loss are tested against WRN and SMARCA2 dependency. For each, the claim direction is negative, meaning that if the exposure were broadly associated with dependency it would show a more negative score and therefore stronger dependency. I expect these comparisons to be small or null because WRN has previously appeared relatively selective for MSI-high, and SMARCA2 appears tied to SMARCA4 loss. If BRCA2 loss or TP53 loss produced effects near 0.1 or larger, that would substantially weaken claims of biological specificity and suggest broader DNA-repair or tumor-suppressor-context dependence. This is therefore a falsifiable control rather than a new positive claim.

The MTAP comparisons address co-deletion biology around p53 pathway outcomes. The USP7 association is already supported overall, in adherent culture, adenocarcinoma, the Ky library, and MTAP-loss cells. I now test TP53 loss against USP7 dependency restricted to MTAP-WT cells. This checks whether the USP7 association is merely tied to 9p21-region deletion co-alterations or remains meaningful when MTAP deletion is absent. A positive raw contrast would mean less negative USP7 dependency in TP53-loss cells, i.e. weaker dependency, as accepted for H48. For MDM2, TP53 loss restricted to MTAP-WT cells tests whether p53-MDM2 biology is clearer when MTAP co-deletion is not present. The expected direction is again positive for weaker MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells, but prior main-effect evidence was near zero, so this is a targeted mechanistic-context check rather than a strong positive expectation.

Finally, I register two RAS/PI3K/receptor crosstalk interactions. The KRAS interaction tests whether KRAS mutation effects on KRAS dependency differ in NF1-loss cells. NF1 loss activates RAS signaling, so the effect could be enhanced or redundant; I leave the raw direction uncertain, with a negative claim direction for a possible stronger KRAS dependency. The EGFR interaction tests PIK3CA mutation as a downstream bypass modifier of EGFR-amplification effects on EGFR dependency. The claim direction is positive because downstream PI3K activation would be expected to make the EGFR-amplification contrast less negative, i.e. attenuated upstream receptor dependence. Because prior EGFR amplification main effects were unstable, this is exploratory pathway-redundancy testing, not a positive biological claim. All proposed comparisons are associations within the supplied dataset and validation structure, not causal driver statements or externally generalizable clinical biomarker claims.

There are no assessments_due at this analyze stage, so I am not changing any existing claim status. The analysis budget is allocated to untested claims that most directly test robustness, specificity, and pathway confounding around the independently supported core associations. H101 and H102 directly estimate the MSI-high WRN effect and the TP53-loss USP7 effect within high Cas9 screens; large signed effects there would strengthen the interpretation that these core associations are not confined to low-Cas9 screens, while attenuated effects would require narrowing them. H103 through H106 and H99 through H100 form a specificity battery for WRN and SMARCA2 using BRCA2 loss, TP53 loss, and STK11 loss. These are expected to be small if WRN dependency is relatively specific to MSI-high and SMARCA2 dependency is relatively specific to SMARCA4 loss; sizable effects would indicate broader tumor-suppressor, DNA-repair, or lung adenocarcinoma co-alteration dependence. H109 tests the USP7 association in MTAP-WT cells, addressing whether the accepted TP53-loss USP7 result is merely a consequence of 9p21-region co-deletion, while H110 tests the same MTAP-WT context for MDM2 dependency. These are exploratory pathway-redundancy checks. I will interpret the results conservatively: for core-like effects, I will require signed estimates with interval bounds clearly above the practical ~0.1 dependency-score benchmark; small intervals crossing zero will be treated as null context checks. All findings remain dataset-specific associations, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable clinical biomarkers.

The new discovery results strongly reinforce the accepted core associations in important measured contexts, while most specificity and pathway-crosstalk controls are null. H101 estimates the MSI-high effect on WRN dependency within high-Cas9 screens: signed estimate +0.789, interval +0.744 to +0.834, direction -1. Because the signed hypothesis is for stronger dependency in MSI-high cells, this means MSI-high screens have more negative WRN scores even when cas9_activity_pct is at least 75%. The interval is far above the practical ~0.1 benchmark, so I accept H101 and close it as a robust context-specific confirmation of H11. H102 estimates the TP53-loss effect on USP7 dependency within high-Cas9 screens: signed estimate +0.807, interval +0.779 to +0.836, direction +1. This is a large positive raw contrast, meaning TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, consistent with accepted H48 and robust to Cas9 performance. I accept H102 and close it.

H109 similarly shows that the TP53-loss/USP7 association is not confined to MTAP-deleted contexts: in MTAP-WT cells, signed estimate +0.815, interval +0.792 to +0.838. This substantially reduces concern that the USP7 association is a byproduct of 9p21/MTAP co-deletion. I accept H109 and close it. These large stratum-specific effects do not need independent validation because their discovery intervals are extremely precise, exceed the clinical-significance threshold by a large margin, and are aligned with already independently validated core effects.

The specificity battery for WRN is essentially null: BRCA2 loss on WRN H103 is -0.002 with interval -0.050 to +0.046; TP53 loss on WRN H105 is -0.009 with interval -0.039 to +0.022; STK11 loss on WRN H99 is -0.010 with interval -0.038 to +0.019. None reach the practical benchmark and all intervals include clinically trivial effects, so I reject these as completed specificity checks. H100, STK11 loss on SMARCA2, is +0.0045 [-0.038, +0.047], and H106, TP53 loss on SMARCA2, is -0.021 [-0.062, +0.021]; both are null and do not undermine the SMARCA4-loss specificity of SMARCA2 dependency.

The only borderline result is H104, BRCA2 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.0675, interval -0.0055 to +0.1406. With direction -1, the positive signed estimate corresponds to raw more negative SMARCA2 scores in BRCA2-loss cells, i.e. stronger dependency. This is in the same direction as accepted SMARCA4-loss biology, but the point estimate is below the 0.1 practical benchmark and the interval includes zero; however, the upper bound extends beyond the threshold. Because this is a specificity-relevant signal rather than a core pathway effect already repeatedly confirmed, it is the most scientifically useful candidate for independent validation. I therefore keep H104 unresolved and active and request validation for H104. Validation will test whether BRCA2 loss genuinely broadens the context of SMARCA2 dependency or whether the borderline positive interval is noise under multiplicity.

The remaining pathway-crosstalk checks are not supported. H107, KRAS mutation by NF1-loss interaction for KRAS dependency, is +0.054 [-0.017, +0.125]; H108, EGFR amplification by PIK3CA-mutation interaction for EGFR dependency, is +0.026 [-0.063, +0.116]; and H110, TP53-loss MTAP-WT effect on MDM2, is +0.003 [-0.027, +0.032]. These point estimates are below the practical benchmark, intervals include zero, prior main effects or related checks were weak/null, and multiplicity argues against accepting them as meaningful crosstalk or pathway modifiers. I reject H107, H108, and H110 and close them as completed exploratory checks. Overall, the evidence continues to support four large, independently replicated dataset-specific associations: MSI-high/stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss/stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-loss/weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with strong robustness to high Cas9 activity and MTAP status. All remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or clinically generalizable claims.

At this synthesis, H13 reaches its validation response deadline and is explicitly reassessed. The KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association is accepted and closed. Discovery R7 and independent validation R65 are both large, positive signed estimates, about +0.797 and +0.804, with lower bounds +0.776 and +0.773. Because the hypothesis direction is positive, these signed positive values correspond to raw less negative NFE2L2 dependency scores in KEAP1-loss cells, meaning weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The effect is far above the conservative 0.1 dependency-score benchmark and also far above any plausible 10 percent threshold relative to the scale of the outcome, so it is scientifically meaningful within this dataset. This remains an association in the supplied data and validation split, not proof of causality or generalizable clinical biology. H104 was sent for validation to test whether BRCA2 loss broadens SMARCA2 dependency beyond SMARCA4-loss contexts. It fails validation and is rejected. Discovery R83 was only borderline in the hypothesized stronger-dependency direction, signed +0.0675 with interval -0.0055 to +0.1406. Independent validation R92 is opposite, signed -0.0579 with interval -0.1608 to +0.0449. The signed negative validation means raw BRCA2-loss cells had less negative SMARCA2 scores relative to comparator cells, contrary to the stronger-dependency claim. A simple inverse-variance synthesis would place the combined effect near +0.026 with interval roughly within +/-0.06, clinically trivial. Therefore BRCA2 loss is not accepted as a validated SMARCA2 dependency modifier. This strengthens specificity of the accepted SMARCA4-loss association, though it does not exclude all DNA-repair context effects. H8, the main TP53-loss contrast for MDM2, is now rejected and closed. R8 is signed +0.0085 with interval -0.0181 to +0.0350, too small for practical or clinical significance; together with the null MTAP-WT TP53-loss MDM2 check H110, there is no support for a simple overall MDM2 main association with TP53 status in this dataset. The independently supported core remains four dataset-specific associations: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H11; SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H12; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, H48; and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H13. Each has discovery and validation estimates near 0.8 signed units, with lower bounds far above meaningful thresholds. These core effects also persist in several measured contexts, including high-Cas9 screens, MTAP-WT cells, adenocarcinoma, adherent culture, Ky library, and ARID1A-loss cells. Negative and null results are informative because many broad alternatives are not supported: receptor and pathway crosstalk contrasts involving KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, and PIK3CA are weak or unstable; MYC amplification is not associated with POLR2A, USP7, DHX9, or validated KIF18A effects; most technical or constructed-marker interactions are small; and many tumor-suppressor or co-alteration checks for TP53, MTAP, CDKN2A, KEAP1, BRCA2, STK11, ARID1A, and SMARCA4 cross-links are null or inconsistent. The most informative next analysis is to complete the remaining targeted p53/ARF/MDM2 and DNA-repair specificity battery: H73 and H74 test BRCA2 loss on DHX9 and POLR2A, H83 tests BRCA2 loss on KIF18A, H75 tests CDKN2A loss on MDM2, H86 tests MDM2 TP53-loss modification by CDKN2A loss, and H72 tests the SMARCA4-loss ARID1A interaction for SMARCA2. If these are null, they should be closed; if any produces a replicated absolute effect around or above the practical benchmark, it will require a narrower claim about the relevant dependency context. Receptor crosstalk and TMED10 or TMED10/ERBB2 checks are deferred as lower priority because prior related effects were small, unstable, or not replicated.
